title: Kotodama: a new grammar game from scratch
question: This is a playable prototype, not pictures: play it at https://fumbleforce.github.io/tower-of-words/game3d/minigames/kotodama.html (phone or desktop, about four minutes). It's a new game, started over after "even less fun, start over, write a new game from scratch, make it the most fun and impressive grammar game in existence". Is this fun?

media.caption: Frame strip, phone: the first と combo in shift 2. ケンジくんと モリさんに コーヒーを だしてください: the lights dip, the command rises off the vending machine, two cans fly, both bubbles pop, then 2 × 2 with the streak and ください multipliers.
Frame strip, phone: the particles swapped on purpose. コーヒーに ミオさんを だして puts Mio out of the vending machine and lands her on the coffee, then one line says what を and に said.

options.label: kotodama: fun, keep going with it
options.note: The pitch: B2 after six, and the old machines do exactly what Eric says, word for word. You build each command from the room itself (tap who and what, give each a particle, then fire the verb), and the particles decide what flies where. Requests pile up faster than one command can answer them one at a time, so と (two or three people served in one sentence) is the combo you need, scored 2 × 2 or 3 × 3 with a streak on top. Between shifts you pick a power word: も, みんな, まって or ください. Three shifts, three hearts, a daily run with a best score. The design page, with what it borrows and an honest check, is game3d/minigames/README.md (Kotodama). The screens come from a headless run of the daily seed; the frame strips are from game3d/minigames/tools/frames.mjs.
